proposals.premise: Treat the changing bend as a layered surface: three records can be related by place and era without implying that the river kept the same shape.
proposals.opening: Desktop shows the ferry photo beside a vertical 1932–2025 record rail; phone shows the photo first, followed by the rail. Source and uncertainty labels share each record.
proposals.move: Selecting the 1978 mark reveals its scan and east-abutment note in an adjacent panel on desktop and directly below on phone.
proposals.tradeoff: Spatial layering makes relationships tactile and immediate, but requires explicit warnings that the ferry-era bend differs from the present one.

proposals.premise: Use an archive-table reading order: photo, mark and sound remain separate source objects, while repeated bend labels invite careful comparison rather than false alignment.
proposals.opening: Desktop opens with three wide record rows sharing a source drawer; phone stacks compact record cards. The 2025 audio card pairs playback with its transcript control.
proposals.move: Pressing play starts the 18-second public-steps recording; progress and transcript appear within the same row or expanded phone card.
proposals.tradeoff: This direction keeps provenance and uncertainty unusually clear, including the unverified photographer, but offers less atmospheric continuity between the three eras.
